units.text: A brass and glass chamber at the top of a stone tower, the great lens turning slowly above.
Wind hums in the lantern panes.
SILAS PENHALLOW, fifties, the head keeper, stands at the logbook with a pen.
THADDEUS MARROW, twenties, his assistant, kneels at the lens with an oilcan.
HOBART VANE, forties, a Trinity House inspector in a wet greatcoat, stands in the doorway with his hat in his hands.
Mr. Vane, you've climbed a hundred and forty steps in a gale to tell me my lamp is dim.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: I climbed them to see whether it was.
units.name: HOBART

units.text: It's not dim, sir. Silas trims the wick every hour.
units.name: THADDEUS

units.text: He needn't, but he does, Mr. Marrow. That's a good habit in a young man.
units.name: HOBART

units.text: Thaddeus wipes the oilcan on his sleeve and does not look up.
Hobart, you'll take tea before you go down.
units.name: SILAS

units.text: Silas and Hobart face each other.
Thaddeus stands, crosses to it, and lights the spirit stove.
Behind him the lens turns, and the beam sweeps the three of them with white light, and goes out over the black water.
